value.referent: CDC blood lead reference value of 3.5 μg/dL

ev.q: This report describes BLLs above the CDC blood lead reference value (BLRV) of 3.5 μ g/dL among five NYC residents
child B’s BLL had declined from 18 to 14 μ g/dL, child C’s from 30 to 22 μ g/dL, and the mother’s from 14 to 8 μ g/dL

changes.why: `across` should name the variables compared (person and time), not the referent itself; framework and null scale are kept.

equity.level_reason: Immigrant origin (Pakistan; South Asian and other immigrant communities) describes the family and surma users, and the implications note cultural ties abroad delaying follow-up, but no group results are compared in this single-family case series.

level_alternative.reason: Nativity only defines the case population (an immigrant family), which under the level-0 rule does not raise the level.

ev.q: routine testing detected a BLL of 15 μ g/dL in an asymptomatic child, aged 4 years (child A), who had arrived from Pakistan 16 months earlier
surma is often purchased abroad by South Asian, Middle Eastern, and North- and West-African immigrants and hand-carried into the United States
Persons with cultural connections abroad, and who use products such as surma, might also be more likely to have extended absences
Lead Poisoning in a Mother and Her Four Children Using a Traditional Eye Cosmetic

determinants_of_health.v: deeply ingrained cultural practices; testing mandates; extended travel abroad delaying follow-up

ev.q: challenges of risk communication when deeply ingrained cultural practices, such as the use of surma, persist despite health warnings
effectiveness of blood lead surveillance depends on testing mandates, and might miss populations at risk of lead exposure who do not routinely receive testing

equity.equity_measurement: Single immigrant family; no comparison group or rates by nativity or any other SPD.

notes: Agree with the structural record otherwise: limited data focus, case series, BLL trajectories set side by side against the BLRV with no procedures or inference.
